The bare fragments were left unmapped without queries. Damaged-head entries were mapped only when the sub-term named a single unambiguous structure, e.g. '— espinoso' to foramen spinosum.

Mappings accepted on UBERON's own exact synonym or label where the class name differs from the usual term: 'Cerebelo — amígdala' to paraflocculus (exact synonym 'cerebellar tonsil'); 'Seno — recto' to tentorial sinus (the definition describes the straight sinus); 'Nervio(s) — intermedio' to 'sensory root of facial nerve' (matched by label; 'nervus intermedius' appears only among its non-exact synonyms); 'Arteria(s) — carótida — común' to 'common carotid artery plus branches' (exact synonym 'common carotid artery'); 'Tálamo' to dorsal thalamus (the human UBERON subset has no plain 'thalamus' class).
Every mapping is matchKind 'exact'; none needed 'laterality_dropped'.

The human UBERON subset has no class for many common head structures (e.g. sphenopalatine artery, mandibular fossa, pterygopalatine fossa, frontal bone, supraorbital and supratrochlear nerves, diploic and emissary veins), so those entries stay unmapped with a Spanish reason.
